title: SYNTHETIC: Effect of compound ZX-101 on resting heart rate (toy RCT)

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: This synthetic trial tests a fictional compound, ZX-101. We randomized 200 fictional adults to ZX-101 or placebo. Resting heart rate fell by 6 beats per minute in the treatment arm (p = 0.01). No serious adverse events were recorded.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Participants were aged 40 to 65 and had no prior cardiac disease. Randomization was 1:1 and blinded, as described in Fig. 1. Heart rate was measured at baseline and at week 12 by trained staff. Analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle, e.g. all randomized participants were included. Missing data were handled by multiple imputation.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Mean baseline heart rate was 74 beats per minute in both arms. At week 12 the ZX-101 arm averaged 68 and the placebo arm averaged 74. The difference was statistically significant. Mild nausea occurred in 9% of treated participants versus 3% on placebo.

title: SYNTHETIC: ZX-101 and heart rate in older adults (toy cohort)

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: In a fictional cohort of 1,000 adults over 70, ZX-101 users showed no meaningful change in resting heart rate. Observational confounding cannot be excluded.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Heart rate differed by 1 beat per minute between users and non-users (p = 0.40). Results were similar across sexes. Adherence was self-reported, which limits interpretation.

title: SYNTHETIC: Review of heart rate lowering compounds (toy review)

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: This fictional review summarizes evidence on heart rate lowering compounds. Evidence for ZX-101 is mixed, with one randomized trial and one cohort study pointing in different directions.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Randomized evidence is generally stronger than observational evidence for causal claims. Differences in age range between studies may explain the discordant findings. Larger trials are needed.
